principle.statement: Before authoring new content/code to address a real problem, (1) search for real, already-existing artifacts that may already satisfy the requirement; (2) verify SUBSTANCE, not just a name/label/category match -- a filename or categorical hit is a lead to investigate, never proof of relevance by itself; (3) only if no substantively relevant artifact is found, author new content -- reusing what already exists otherwise.
principle.anti_surface_matching_clause: A candidate artifact found via name/label/category matching alone MUST NOT be treated as satisfying step 1 until its actual content is checked against the real requirement. Required because a real application of this principle (PHASE-E22) found 2 filename matches (PHASE-494/503, "*reclassif*") that were confirmed, by content, to be entirely unrelated to the real task at hand.

confidence_method: base(0.5, reused unmodified from E21/E5) + corroboration_bonus(min(0.4, 0.1*(3-1)))=0.20, capped at 0.9.
enforcement_status: NOT_ENFORCED -- this is a recognized, evidenced, domain-independent development principle available for voluntary future reference; it is not (yet) a mandatory rule, lint check, or CI gate. Adopting it as binding is a separate, future decision.
